analysis:
All four units are documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md head excerpts (lines 1414-2008, historical release notes) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump plus a new 'Calibration ownership and foreground admission' section at ~lines 335-362 and a new file-map row at ~line 412). No source, wire-protocol, key-handling, attestation or authorization code is changed. The unit d25347f864a05087:0 carries only metadata (modified, mode 100644 both sides, no content), nothing security-relevant.

The doc text claims provider-local behavior: calibration uses existing KV/service budgets and does not lower reserves or raise concurrency limits. Foreground customer requests cancel calibration and wait for actual retirement before admission. Calibration observations are staged per cell and published only after the completion posture check passes, so cancelled or non-nominal cells discard them. Calibration samples do not increment served-request or output-token totals. Capacity wire fields and the platform memory contract are stated unchanged. The cited files (IdleCalibrationCoordinator.swift, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibrationRequests.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift) were not supplied, so the described behavior is unverified. The next pass should check these source changes for calibration-probe lifecycle and availability (T-010, T-029): foreground-lease wait bounded by deadlines, no starvation of consumers, no reservation leaks if a probe wedges. It should also check that calibration prompts are synthetic and never touch A-001 or the prefix cache (T-041) or donate to the SSD tier.

No threat-model update is needed from these docs alone; the changelog text references T-051, which is outside the supplied definitions.
